messages:
alex: Heads-up — I found a divergence between the Python SDK and the raw REST contract for POST /v1/generate. Py SDK is serializing None into explicit nulls, whereas the REST examples assume omitted params mean server default. Example payloads below.

alex: Python (current behavior):
```py
# payload sent over the wire
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha",
  "max_tokens": null,
  "temperature": 0.7
}
```

alex: TypeScript SDK (current behavior):
```ts
// payload sent over the wire
{
  model: 'redwood-alpha',
  temperature: 0.7 // maxTokens is omitted entirely
}
```

maria: Right — server treats missing as default, but explicit nulls are interpreted differently (backend validates and sometimes rejects). We should avoid sending null for optional numeric params.

sam: Sounds like the issue is in the Python request serializer (dataclass -> dict). We include keys even when fields are None. Quick fix: drop keys with value is None before json.dumps.

jordan: Agree. Also watch enums/empty lists — dropping vs empty list semantics differ. For numeric/optional fields like max_tokens/temperature we should omit when None.

infra-bot: telemetry: found ~43k requests in last 30d with explicit null for max_tokens and ~11k for stop_sequences null. Most come from two API keys (customer A and internal e2e tests).

maria: Good catch on stop_sequences. For arrays we must preserve empty array vs omit. Need a whitelist of fields where None->omit is safe.

sam: Proposed serializer change (patch):
```py
# simplified
payload = {k: v for k, v in dataclass_as_dict(req).items() if v is not None}
# then json.dumps(payload)
```
Add an allowlist for fields that must keep null/empty.

alex: I'll open a PR with the change + unit tests for generate/embeddings and an integration run against staging. PR: https://repo/repo/pull/1234

devex: Please add a changelog note and an entry in SDK release notes about tightening serialization; mention the risk for customers who intentionally sent explicit nulls.

jordan: Also add an e2e test hitting the server to confirm behavior (server defaults applied when omitted).

sam: I can review the PR tomorrow morning. Can we also add a feature-flagged rollout so we can revert if we see regressions?

alex: Plan: feature-flag rollout, unit + e2e tests, telemetry alert to catch spike in 5xx or validation errors. I'll include a migration note and request reviews from @maria and @sam.

maria: :thumbsup: Sounds good. One more ask — create a tiny compatibility test that replays recorded requests that had nulls to ensure no customer breaks.

alex: Will do. Thanks — ping me if you see any related customer tickets. :eyes:
